result.title: When Exact Token Importance Is Not Enough: Limits of Top-K Selection in LLM Attention
result.summary: Long-context language models often retain only a limited set of past token positions for an attention query. A common strategy scores positions individually and keeps the highest-ranked K. Yet attention weights are renormalized over the chosen set: two individually important positions need not form the best pair. We ask whether independent ranking suffices even when each importance score measures the exact downstream change in next-token predictions caused by deleting that position alone. It does not. A four-position construction makes the ranked pair incur 133.2 times the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence of the optimal pair, and a parametric family proves that this multiplicative gap is unbounded. An exact exchange identity and preference reversals for every K >= 2 explain the interaction. In exhaustive frozen-model audits of SmolLM2, Gemma, and Qwen, exact-singleton Top-4 leaves at least 10% relative improvement within a fully enumerated 24-position candidate pool in 55/60, 49/60, and 60/60 cases, respectively. SwapCert, a same-budget one-swap audit, detects 157/164 such cases and returns directly checkable improving supports. A KL-margin certificate relates support fidelity to next-token stability; larger-budget, multi-layer cached-decoding experiments measure predictive fidelity at K = 128 and 256. These results establish joint support quality as an essential object of analysis for sparse attention and motivate downstream-aware support selection under inference constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究长上下文注意力中「逐位置打分取 Top-K」的局限：即使每个位置的删除效应被精确度量，独立排序也会因注意力重归一化而错失联合最优支持集，并提出同预算的 SwapCert 审计检验可改进位置。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本注意力稀疏化工作，但其「单点重要性不等于联合支持质量」的论证与审计方法，可能可为 LVR 中视觉证据/隐状态筛选及 KV 缓存保留的评价提供核查线索，需确认视觉场景下的可迁移性。
